audit_claims.direction_explanation: The numerical point estimate and its interval become absent; this is not evidence that the intervention is safe or ineffective.

departing_trials.source_excerpt: Adverse reactions were consistent with the previously reported risks associated with canagliflozin except for an increased risk of amputation (6.3 vs. 3.4 participants per 1000 patient-years; hazard ratio, 1.97; 95% CI, 1.41 to 2.75); amputations were primarily at the level of the toe or metatarsal. Conclusions In two trials involving patients with type 2 diabetes and an elevated risk of cardiovascular disease, patients treated with canagliflozin had a lower risk of cardiovascular events than those who received placebo but a greater risk of amputation, primarily at the level of the toe or metatarsal. (Funded by Janssen Research and Development; CANVAS and CANVAS-R ClinicalTrials.gov numbers, NCT01032629 and NCT01989754 , respectively.).

direction_policy: Estimate-absence transitions take precedence: numeric to absent RESULT_REMOVED; absent to numeric RESULT_ADDED; both absent NO_DIRECTION even if candidate k changes. For two numerical results, AWAY_FROM_NULL takes priority if any of larger absolute effect (absolute log ratio or absolute MD), narrower comparable CI, more favourable point, or newly favourable CI applies. Mixed signals are disclosed. A newly favourable CI with no prior CI is a new claim, never a computed narrowing. Otherwise weakening is TOWARD_NULL; unchanged point with membership change is MEMBERSHIP_ONLY. All outcomes here favour lower values except ovulation, which favours higher odds; harm disappearance is flagged for presentation favourability, never treated as evidence of safety.
